rule: Use a skill for instructed procedures, a hook for lifecycle reactions, a plugin for tools or services, and a mod only for live engine or terminal replacement.

packages.why_mod: Owns live workflow selection, contract gates, candidate checks, and task decisions through generic host services and bounded receipts.

Owns the Claude CLI model catalog, request translation and ask_claude delegation over a host-approved provider service while the native host executes every tool and keeps permissions, accounting and cancellation.
Replaces the live terminal inspector dialog and refresh actions while reading generic task, contract, ledger, and install identity state.
Drives live native agent spawning, waiting, result consumption, and lifecycle state inside the active task.
Alters admitted model requests and the live response stream, which hooks and plugins cannot replace.
Runs a granted program outside the session sandbox with host-supervised lifecycle and revocation.
Replaces live compaction and context recovery policy.
Replaces the model, provider, and reasoning preset selected at the live request boundary.
Replaces live terminal layout, theme, render templates, and key handling.
Registers and restricts a host-enforced workflow contract during a live task without owning native guarantees.
Exercises the bounded context observer API only; user-facing guidance belongs in a skill or lifecycle hook.
Exercises tool, command, progress, and durable-state conformance only; a user-facing counter would be a plugin tool.
Exercises input and lifecycle replacement conformance only; a user-facing deterministic guard would be a hook.
Exercises simple tool interception conformance only; user-facing tool policy belongs in a hook or plugin.
Exercises a host-routed service import only; a user-facing service consumer belongs in a plugin.
Exercises a host-routed service export only; a user-facing service belongs in a plugin.
Draws the Oh My Diff wordmark and launch status into the terminal header from the read-only launch identity.
Selects the compact native model and reasoning picker presentation while native keeps rows, warnings and persistence.

Times pending approvals and questions from public app_server_request events and answers expired ones through the generic app.respond operation, which can only decline, deny or answer; active by default in OMD+.
Arms a timer from public model_response telemetry and starts compaction through the routed thread/compact/start app-server method when the prompt cache is about to expire; active by default in OMD+.

Draws a configurable status line in the generic below- or above-composer site from public telemetry, exec and HTTP grants; it turns off the native status row through built-in controls only while active; active by default in OMD+.
Owns a render hook on the generic tool_call site that draws one line per agent tool call; the host keeps the native row, its expansion and copy; active by default in OMD+.
Pins Codex's own update_plan steps above the composer from app notifications; adds no model tool.
A user-typed /continue command that submits a resume instruction with the host-recorded turn activity.
Exercises reusable live workspace read, pre-rename events and host-authorized transactions.

Owns live language-server synchronization, post-edit diagnostic feedback and rename/edit planning through generic host process, workspace and tool-output operations; exports the omd.lsp query service for the code-intelligence view.
Registers an independent virtual resource using the shared sandboxed extension bridge; the provider owns its resource grammar and content.
Demonstrates scoped fact selection and frozen live context reuse, plus commands through the same public bridge.
Owns a bounded completed-turn procedure and result interpretation through the shared accounted review interface.
Uses only a public tool export and a granted generic service request; no live engine replacement.

An independent author package that uses only the host primitives: a contract document, receipts, sandboxed commands, workspace listing, durable store and evidence, stream control, built-in controls and a list replacement.
Demonstrates live frozen-workspace review, scoped restrictions, receipts, and resumable agent evidence using only the public mod API.

Owns on-demand, triggered and completed-turn advice, the opt-in important-output observer, independent review prompts, typed result and citation validation, deduplication and selected-context presentation through public accounted review primitives.
Suggests the rest of a recent prompt as revision-bound ghost text from draft change events, which skills and hooks cannot draw.
Rewrites or refuses pasted draft text through the composer_edit interceptor chain before it reaches the draft.
Approves routine check commands inside a user-delegated native approval grant, which hooks and skills cannot hold.
Refuses or restricts other mods at load and guards host requests under a user-granted policy, which hooks and skills cannot do.
Rewrites slash-command and settings metadata, arguments and writes through host continuations that hooks and skills cannot reach.
Publishes and receives namespaced in-process channel events between live mods.
Asks the user through native text and confirmation prompts from a live command.
Replaces the model-bound request history at each request without changing the transcript.
Appends composable feedback to live tool output before it reaches the model.
Replaces live composer mention ranking inside the terminal.
Keeps thread-scoped state that forks and deletes with the live thread.
Lists the session's built-in and mod slash commands from the live terminal inventory.
Lists the TCP listeners of the current session's background terminals from the live host.
Keeps inline scrollback free of every mod sidebar and header for screen readers and plain terminals.
Renders an imported image inside a live terminal render site and opens links after native confirmation.
Redacts credentials from history text in the host's persistence path before the rollout is written.
Replaces the live terminal layout with splits, tabs, documents and diffs.
Ports Claude Code's Tag Client example to a component module that posts pointer clicks to its hooks.
Draws bordered cards, flat filled panels, flex rows, hover and focus accents and a gapped split layout with the box model.
Shows the attached-client roster and launches its own text renderer process that joins the session over the client protocol.
Keeps a filterable approval desk beside other sidebars, with a client adapter that answers approvals over the client protocol.
Redraws native terminal components: a custom spinner, framed tool calls, annotated assistant messages and a wrapped question.
Keeps a form, a streamed status and a derived summary on keyed reactive state.
Turns live app-server notifications into terminal notifications with focus state.
Drives package controls behind native confirmation from a live terminal panel.
Selects credential-bound routes at the live request boundary.
Merges parallel-safe tool calls of one live response into a single call.
Writes binary evidence and attaches it to the live composer.
Runs a sandboxed interactive shell rendered inside a live terminal pane.
Defines a model-visible tool at run time and refreshes its answer from a keyed timer.
Enrolls origin-bound secrets through native prompts and hands them only to its sidecars.
Runs one-shot completions on configured worker routes under live admission and the ledger.
Defers and re-describes model-visible tool specs per route through the composable tool_specs chain.
Pages the latest repository session's tool calls and results through the host's scoped session reader.
Caches, confirms and retries live tool calls through the continuation chain and the turn's tool executor.
Reads the host turn-activity ledger for the live thread.
Watches workspace paths and reports external changes through live terminal notifications.
Starts a live thread bound to a permitted worktree root and shows it in the terminal.
Owns the plan-mode removal policy through public builtins controls (hidden /plan, disabled plan mode, turn-start clamp); enabled by default in OMD+.

Owns the user-typed /preview command, its packaged Markdown renderer, file watches, the inline preview dialog, inline Mermaid drawings of assistant messages and draft image thumbnails above the composer; installed inactive in OMD+.

Owns the /mods screen, its actions and the first-run card over public package controls and terminal sites; native code keeps trust, confirmation, package authority and /omd recovery; enabled by default in both profiles.

Owns the update notice, the /update dialog, snooze and skip state and the update policy settings (checks, channel, cadence, pin, automatic updates); the installer reads those settings and does the network check and installation; active in OMD Core and OMD+.

Owns secret and PII detection, sensitive-path rules, reviewed exemptions and salted placeholders as a required model_send policy and approval middleware over the generic final-request stage; installed inactive in OMD+.

Owns the provider usage HUD: a per-thread request ledger from model_response, cache, cost and quota classification, the usage and workers row above the composer, the usage dialog and the summary the theme draws; installed inactive in OMD+.
Owns the user-invoked code-intelligence view, its request hop, result navigation over the omd.lsp service, file-view diagnostics and the on-demand language-server pane; installed inactive in OMD+.
Owns @ mention ranking through the exclusive completion replacement, queues paths from submitted input and learns them at turn start into repository storage; installed inactive in OMD+.
Refreshes source-bound repository facts against the current workspace and stores revision-checked evidence and approved lessons for later tasks; installed inactive in OMD+.
Owns the Python-facing context, child-agent and refinement API plus a versioned session harness in the model-bound request view; installed inactive in OMD+.
Owns the Cursor SDK transport, custom-tool relay of OMD tools, usage settlement log, in-session setup and /cursor diagnostics over a host-approved provider service; installed inactive in OMD+.
Owns the mini presentation of omd mini sessions: a short prompt, one status line and the switch request read by the launcher; installed inactive in OMD+.

Owns which parallel read calls merge through the exclusive tool_batch replacement, the merged tool that runs each distinct original once through tools.invoke, and code-mode read reuse as a tool interceptor over structured values shared through its repository store; installed inactive in OMD+.

Owns schema-aware argument repair as a tool interceptor and JSON syntax repair as a response_stream interceptor, with evidence records and loop limits; host admission revalidates every rewrite; installed inactive in OMD+.

Owns profile selection, setup guidance, paid-route consent and status over host credential flows and routes.select, plus the loopback router that adapts Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages providers; installed inactive in OMD+.

synthetic_fixtures.name: reader
synthetic_fixtures.reason: Exercises bounded Pi resource discovery and command coexistence; a user-facing reader belongs in a plugin with skills.

synthetic_fixtures.name: tool
synthetic_fixtures.reason: Exercises duplicate tool slots, progress, and reload boundaries; a user-facing tool belongs in a plugin.
